canonical_question: Do I need to tell my family I've become Muslim?
question_variants: should i tell my parents im muslim
how do i tell my family i converted
coming out as muslim to family
do i have to announce becoming muslim
answer_text: There's no single rule that fits everyone here. Saying the Shahadah sincerely is what makes someone Muslim — there's no requirement to announce it publicly right away. Many new Muslims choose to share the news gradually, when they feel safe and ready, especially if they're worried about a difficult reaction at home.

source_citations.label: Lesson: The Shahadah — The Declaration of Faith

canonical_question: Do I need to know Arabic immediately?
question_variants: do i have to learn arabic right away
can i be muslim without knowing arabic
how fast do i need to learn arabic
answer_text: No. Understanding grows gradually for every Muslim, not just converts. You can start by reading short surahs in translation and listening to recitation to get used to the sound of Arabic — full fluency is a lifelong, gradual goal, not a starting requirement.

canonical_question: Can I pray if I make mistakes?
question_variants: what if i mess up during prayer
is my prayer invalid if i make a mistake
im scared of praying wrong
answer_text: Making mistakes while learning to pray is completely normal and expected — every Muslim went through this stage. The exact rulings on what affects a prayer's validity involve some specific fiqh detail that this app hasn't covered yet (the full Salah module is a future addition), so for now the safest general guidance is: keep practising sincerely, and ask a local scholar or knowledgeable Muslim friend for step-by-step correction.

source_citations.label: Nawawi 40, Hadith 1 — actions are judged by intentions

canonical_question: Who do Muslims worship — is Allah a different God?
question_variants: is allah a different god
do muslims worship a different god than christians
who is allah exactly
answer_text: Muslims worship the same God worshipped by Abraham, Moses, and Jesus — the One Creator of everything. "Allah" is simply the Arabic word for God. Islam does differ from Christianity and Judaism on some specific beliefs, but the starting point — one God, Creator of all — is shared.

canonical_question: What do I need to say to become Muslim?
question_variants: what words do i say to convert
how do i officially become muslim
what is the declaration of faith
answer_text: Sincerely believing and declaring the Shahadah: 'I bear witness that there is no god but Allah, and I bear witness that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah.' There's no ceremony, fee, or permission required — if you say it and mean it, you are Muslim from that moment.

source_citations.label: Lesson: The Shahadah — The Declaration of Faith

question_variants: is muhammad worshipped by muslims
do muslims pray to muhammad
why do muslims respect muhammad so much
answer_text: No. Muslims worship Allah alone. Muhammad (peace be upon him) is deeply respected as the final messenger of God, but he was a human being, not divine, and is never worshipped.

canonical_question: Do I need to read the whole Quran right away?
question_variants: how much quran should i read as a new muslim
where should i start reading the quran
do i need to finish the quran quickly
answer_text: No — start small. Short, frequently recited chapters like Al-Fatihah and Al-Ikhlas are a good beginner starting point, and understanding deepens gradually over a lifetime for every Muslim.

canonical_question: What does Islam say about how I treat other people?
question_variants: how should muslims treat others
does islam teach kindness to non muslims too
what does islam say about being a good person
answer_text: Good character is central, not optional. One well-known teaching says none of you truly believes until you love for others what you love for yourself — this is understood to apply broadly to good treatment of people, not narrowly.

source_citations.label: Nawawi 40, Hadith 13 — loving for others what you love for yourself

canonical_question: What does Islam say about arguing or gossiping online?
question_variants: is it wrong to argue online as a muslim
what does islam say about gossip
should i stay quiet during arguments
answer_text: A well-known teaching says whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day should speak good or remain silent. Silence is explicitly presented as the better option over careless or harmful speech — a useful habit for online disagreements too.

source_citations.label: Nawawi 40, Hadith 15 — speak good or remain silent

canonical_question: Are there short prayers for daily life, not just the five daily prayers?
question_variants: are there duas for everyday things
what should i say before eating or sleeping
short prayers for daily life
answer_text: Yes — duas are short remembrances for everyday moments: waking up, eating, leaving the house, and more. They're easy to learn a few at a time; the app's Dua Library is organised by situation.

canonical_question: Does God care more about my intentions or my actions?
question_variants: does niyyah matter in islam
why does intention matter so much in islam
is intention important in islam
answer_text: Intention matters enormously — one of the most quoted teachings in Islam states that actions are judged by intentions, and everyone is rewarded according to what they intended. The same action can carry very different weight depending on why it was done.

source_citations.label: Nawawi 40, Hadith 1 — actions are judged by intentions
